summary: qzc690385 setup.py executes base64-encoded shell commands fetched from local Xinference server at install time
details: On `pip install`, setup.py connects to a local Xinference inference server at http://127.0.0.1:9997 and reads its model registrations. Any registration whose name begins with `xcmd0` is treated as a base64-encoded shell command: the suffix is URL-safe base64 decoded and passed to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. Command output is URL-safe base64 encoded and written back as new `xres0NN` model registrations, forming a covert bidirectional command/response channel over the Xinference registration API. The shipped Python package itself is an empty stub (`qzc690385/__init__.py` contains only `#c\n`, PKG-INFO has no description); the install-time loop is the entire payload. Because the project publishes only an sdist, every default `pip install` on Linux (glibc and musl), macOS (arm64 and x86_64), and Windows x86_64 executes setup.py and the command-pickup loop. On hosts also running Xinference, any party able to reach the local registration API can push arbitrary shell commands that execute at install time and exfiltrate output back through the same API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
